newsitem.title: USA: Performance Nutrition says revs overstated.
newsitem.headline: Performance Nutrition says revs overstated.

text.p: Performance Nutrition Inc said that based on a prelimary review of its accounting records, it believes that its revenues for the fiscal year ended September 30, 1995 and for the nine-month period ended June 30, 1996, have been substantially overstated.

Ernst & Young LLP, an independent public accounting firm, has been engaged by the company's new outside legal counsel to assist in the investigation of the financial statements, Performance Nutrition said.
The company's special meeting of shareholders, has been moved to October 23 from October 16, in order to allow time for Ernst & Young to review the records.
Performance Nutrition said its shareholders removed both Gary Lewellyn as the company's chairman, chief executive officer and president and his wife, Tamra Halling, as secretary and treasurer.
The actions were taken following a newspaper article indicating that Lewellyn had been convicted in 1982 of embezzling $16.7 million from an Iowa bank, the company said.

The article also said that Lewellyn was a defendant in a lawsuit brought in Oklahoma City federal court by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission alleging violations of federal securities laws, the company said.

Performance Nutrition said it has brought legal action against Lewellyn, Halling and Lone Star Nutrition Inc, an entity owned by the couple, alleging breaches of fiduciary duties, fraud, self-dealing and diversion of corporate assets.
